title: TikTok Creator Guide: Creator Marketplace, Creator Center, Studio, Shop, and Live Explained
summary: TikTok Creator Marketplace, Creator Center, Studio, Shop, and Live decoded — what each surface does, how to join, who is eligible, and how brands and creators actually work together.
body_markdown:
## Frequently Asked Questions


### Did TikTok pay creators?


Yes, TikTok pays creators through monetization tools such as Creator Marketplace brand partnerships, TikTok Shop affiliate commissions, LIVE gifts, and creator funds where available. Availability varies by country and account, so check the Monetization section in TikTok Studio to see which options your account qualifies for.


### What is the difference between Creator Center and TikTok Studio?


Creator Center refers to TikTok's creator resources and guidance, while TikTok Studio is the in-app destination for managing your account, analytics, and monetization tools. TikTok updates menu labels over time, so always confirm the current names in your own app.


### How do I apply to TikTok Creator Marketplace?


Open TikTok, go to your Profile, tap Menu, open TikTok Studio, select Monetization, then choose Creator Marketplace if it appears and follow the application steps. If the option is missing, access may depend on your location, account status, or TikTok's current requirements.


### What do I need to start TikTok as a creator?


You need a TikTok account, a smartphone with the app installed, and a clear content niche. To access monetization features like Creator Marketplace, you must also meet TikTok's current in-app criteria for your country, account type, and follower activity.


### Who made and owns TikTok?


TikTok is owned by ByteDance, a Chinese technology company that launched the platform in 2016. The company operates TikTok globally, with ByteDance founder Zhang Yiming credited with creating the parent company behind the app.


### Is the TikTok CEO a billionaire?


TikTok's CEO position has changed hands over time, and billionaire status applies to ByteDance founders and early investors rather than the CEO role itself. Zhang Yiming, ByteDance's founder, is widely reported to be a billionaire based on his stake in the company.


### What are the best times to post on TikTok?


The best times to post on TikTok depend on your specific audience, since the algorithm prioritizes engagement over posting time alone. Review your TikTok Studio analytics to identify when your followers are most active, then test posting at those windows consistently.
